title: Polyglot quickstarts: minimal Next.js (Edge), FastAPI, Go HTTP server and CLI cookbook with retry & streaming patterns
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a set of opinionated, minimal starter templates and cookbook snippets that demonstrate best-practice usage patterns for Redwood SDKs across three runtimes: Next.js (Edge + Server), FastAPI (async server), Go HTTP server, and a cross-platform CLI. Focus areas: streaming ergonomics (server push + client streaming), robust retry/backoff strategies for transient errors and rate limits, idempotency patterns for request retries, graceful cancellation and KV cache hints, and small production-safe examples that engineers can copy-paste into apps.
goals: 1) Provide 4 tiny, runnable starters (Next.js edge streaming page, Next.js server-side streaming API, FastAPI async streaming endpoint and client example, Go net/http streaming server/client) + a simple CLI example that streams tokens to stdout with backoff and resume. 2) Document recommended retry settings (exponential backoff with jitter, idempotency keys, retryable status codes) and streaming best practices (chunk framing, reconnection hooks, partial response handling). 3) Include cookbook snippets: batching, prefix caching hints, resumable streams, forced fallback to synchronous mode, and telemetry hooks for Console.
acceptance_criteria:
- Four minimal repositories/examples in /examples/quickstarts with README and get-started steps.
- Each example contains a short README that highlights local dev steps, environment variables, and expected responses.
- Retry and streaming cookbook.md added under docs/cookbooks with concrete code snippets for JS/TS, Python, and Go.
- CI test that runs example servers and a smoke client to assert streaming works end-to-end.
- Performance note: Next.js Edge example demonstrates streaming with <150ms TTFB for first token in local sim.
- Reviewed and approved by PM (Marisol Vega) and Design for sample UX / README clarity.
- PR merged that adds SDK usage patterns to central docs repo and links to Console dashboard example for tracing.
tasks:
- Draft minimal Next.js Edge streaming example and server-side API route.
- Implement FastAPI streaming server and example client with async iterators.
- Implement Go net/http server and client showing context cancellation and chunked responses.
- Implement a cross-platform CLI (TS + Python examples) that streams tokens to stdout, supports --resume and --idempotency-key.
- Write cookbook.md with retry tables, recommended default values, and telemetry integration examples.
- Add unit/smoke CI job to examples CI.
- Create PRs, solicit reviews from SDK leads and runtime team, iterate on feedback.
- Produce a short how-to video (90s) for developer onboarding (optional).
implementation_notes:
- Next.js: use Edge Runtime for streaming HTML fragments using ReadableStream; include an API route showing streaming JSON lines for clients that prefer structured output.
- FastAPI: leverage starlette StreamingResponse with async generator; include background task showing KV cache hint header.
- Go: use http.Flusher to stream incremental JSON or chunked tokens; ensure request context cancellation propagates to the model request.
- CLI: implement a thin wrapper around the SDK streaming client; include robust reconnect logic: exponential backoff with full jitter and a maximum retry cap; persist last-received token offset for --resume.
- Retries: recommend default 3 retries for idempotent requests, 5 seconds base backoff, random jitter 0.5-1.5x; treat 429, 502, 503, 504 as retryable.
- Streaming ergonomics: show both iterator-based consumers and callback-based consumers; include examples for token-by-token rendering and incremental JSON assembly for structured streaming.
- Telemetry: emit a trace/span per example request integrating with Console tracing hooks; include example tags for model, sequence_length, and batching hint.
- Testing: add small harness that mocks the SDK streaming endpoint to assert partial chunk handling and retry behavior.
qa_plan:
- Run smoke tests in CI to validate stream opens and completes under mocked SDK.
- Manual validation: run each example locally following README and verify sample outputs (HTML stream, JSONL, CLI tokens).
- Load test: lightweight local load to ensure Next.js edge starter can handle 10 concurrent streams without blocking.
- PM/Design review of README and UX; incorporate changes.
- Security check: confirm no secrets in examples and environment variable usage documented.
rollout_notes:
- Merge PRs to examples/quickstarts.
- Add links to developer docs landing page and onboarding email.
- Announce in #dev-experience with short gif/demo and link to repo.
- Collect developer feedback for 2 weeks and iterate.
